newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 2.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 2.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
BREMEN - Telecommunications group Deutsche Telekom AG signs sponsoring contract with the German Soccer Federation. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Swedish automaker Volvo is looking for new international lead advertising agency, with top candidates including their German ad agency Gramm, Swedish account holder Forsman & Bodenfors, London-based Abbott Mead Vickers/BBDO, Pirella Goettsche Lowe of Mailand and Euro RSCG of New York and Singapore. (Horizont)

FRANKFURT - Negotiations on the takeover of the 78 percent share of media agency group Debis GFMO appear to be nearly resolved and the German BBDO group is considered the favourite. The shares belonged to GFMO chief executive Dieter Krause before his death in March. (Horizont)

KRONBERG - International advertising sales house IP Network posted six billion marks ($3.5 billion) in turnover worldwide in 1996, a 4.7 percent increase on the previous year, its German unit says. The German IP unit also saw growth in television ad bookings. (Reuter)

BERLIN - German advertising agencies have little chance of playing a key role in the international market, the European chief executive of ad agency J. Walter Thompson, Michael Maedel says. They missed their opportunity when they had it 20 or 30 years ago, he says, and now the concentration of agencies in the industry has progressed too far for them to find a real niche.
(Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

COLOGNE - Germany's number one private television channel RTL says it boosted market share in April while private station Sat1 dropped to third place behind public broadcaster ARD from second place. RTL says its market share rose to 17.8 percent in April from 16.4 percent in the previous month. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Germany's Catholic and Protestant churches issue joint warning against the concentration of media power in the hands of a few and call for greater controls on the Internet. Church leaders have called on business executives and politicians now to allow profit motives and technology alone to drive developments, criticising an increase in the portrayal of sex and violence on television and on computer networks.
(Reuter)
KARLSRUHE - Newsmagazine "Der Spiegel" has the biggest turnover among German magazines, business trade publication Kress Report says. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
RASATT - Mercedes-Benz AG says its new A-class compact car will hit showrooms in October priced at 30,360 marks for the basic 1.4-litre, 82-horsepower "Classic" version. (Reuter)
DARMSTADT - German cosmetics group Wella AG and Italian luxury goods company Gucci N.V. have agreed to expand their cooperation on Gucci perfume promotion, Wella says. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

WALLDORF - Egon Winter will soon become the director of strategic planning at advertising agency Lowe & Partners in Frankfurt. Until he starts in mid-May, he will continue in the same position at DMB&B. (Reuter)
WALLDORF - Mario Canavesi will start as chairman of the German Renault unit on June 1. (Kress)

WALLDORF - Josef Brauner, managing director of Sony's German unit, left the company on April 30, one year earlier than was announced. His successor will be Karl Pohler, who will step in this summer. (Kress)
